# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 105 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 52 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_105_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 105

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever knows father and mother will be called the son of a harlot."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** One of the most enigmatic and shocking sayings in Thomas. Three interpretations have been proposed: (1) The one who comes to know the true divine Father and spiritual Mother will be accused of false parentage by the world (as Jesus was accused of illegitimate birth in John 8:41). (2) The one who recognizes their merely earthly parentage reveals themselves as of mortal, not divine, origin. (3) The paradox is intentional: true spiritual knowledge brings social condemnation.

**"Son of a harlot"** — *porne*: EMET preserves the specific gender (son) and the older English term; PNEUMA's "bastard" is the social consequence (illegitimacy) rather than the Coptic's literal phrase. SOPHIA preserves the literal Coptic.

**Theological Note:** The saying may reflect the early Christian experience of being socially ostracized for claiming divine parentage. No Synoptic parallel exists.
